newsitem.title: HONG KONG: "Warm" PLA no threat to Hong Kong - British general.
newsitem.headline: "Warm" PLA no threat to Hong Kong - British general.

text.p: Chinese troops due to enter Hong Kong on June 30 hours before the midnight handover to Beijing are warm and intelligent people who pose no threat, British Major-General Bryan Dutton said on Tuesday.

The commander of the departing British garrison told reporters at his headquarters that the People's Liberation Army (PLA) would have no internal security role in Hong Kong before or after its return to Chinese rule.
"The Royal Hong Kong Police are in control both before midnight and after midnight," Dutton said.

"The military presence here is purely as a manifestation of sovereignty, a largely ceremonial role. I see no possibility of military of either side being involved in an internal security situation," he said.
Some of Hong Kong's 6.4 million people are wary of the PLA, remembering how it bloodily crushed the 1989 pro-democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square.
Dutton said he had enjoyed a good professional relationship with the PLA and its officers during his three years here.

"As individuals they are warm and intelligent people," he said. "Ultimately they are cautious still because they are children of their system just as I am a child of our system. They are two very difference systems that are still getting to know each other."
On Monday Britain agreed that 509 of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) troops could cross the border at nine p.m. on June 30 in order to be in position in Hnng Kong at midnight.
The Chinese troops will bring pistols and rifles. They are joining an unarmed PLA advance party which has been in Hong Kong for some weeks preparing for the handover.
"They (the PLA) are concerned that they need to be able to do their job and they want to take part in some simple ceremonies here to actually mark the transfer," Dutton said.
"They are only coming over with light personal weapons so they will be in a position to guard their own barracks at midnight. I think that's perfectly acceptable."
Dutton said all PLA troops in Hong Kong would be subject to Hong Kong law and the soldiers who come over next Monday evening would be confined to their barracks until midnight.
The last British soldier is scheduled to leave Hong Kong by air at 3:30 on Tuesday morning.

"I have every confidence in the genuine intentions they have at present," Dutton said. "They have said they want to use Hong Kong as a window on the world to right the image of the PLA. I have confidence that that's a genuine intention."
